right i want you to lock in one thing he mentioned; the educational games.

what if we made a 3D game that would allow someone to playfully learn how codex works in every way? go back and fourth with me on the idea

so this is cute but I need the highest fidelity for the game using the codex logo as the mascot giving you a tour through the codex ecosystem

create a comprehensive plan for how we'll create every aspect of the game, how you'll test AND assess the game in your internal browser before we know it's perfect ready to distribute to my community

and host it on here.now

I want to publish a site using here.now. If I don't have the skill installed yet, read here.now/docs and then install the skill; after installing the skill, ask me what email I signed up with to authenticate me.

I’ve written the [complete production and release plan](</Users/markkashef/Desktop/YouTube/YT Command Centre/projects/codex-learning-game/GAME-PRODUCTION-PLAN.md>) and opened it for review. **here.now is installed and authenticated.**

The proposed game is **Inside Codex**: a cinematic, explorable headquarters where the Codex logo guides players through increasingly useful workflows.

1. **Make the logo the character.**  
   Build the recognizable blue-violet shape and white `>_` in Blender, with sculpted depth, refined materials, expressive hands, and carefully animated gestures. Its personality comes from movement, timing, and voice. We’ll establish the quality bar with a finished arrival scene, mascot close-up, and one playable exhibit.

2. **Build a coherent world around useful lessons.**  
   Three connected wings contain twelve missions:

   | Wing | What players learn |
   |---|---|
   | Understand the system | Model versus harness, context, model/effort selection, permissions |
   | Direct the work | Creating and pinning tasks, forks/worktrees, steering/queueing, reviewing results |
   | Make it repeatable | Skills/plugins, browser testing, automations, packaging and delivery |

   A searchable atlas covers the wider ecosystem. Current documentation and observed app behavior will be recorded separately so we don’t teach installation-specific tricks as universal features.

3. **Make the learning consequential.**  
   Players assemble a practical client-onboarding workflow. Their choices visibly change the environment and the result. They finish with reusable prompts, a context checklist, an AGENTS.md starter, and a handoff checklist. A final unfamiliar task checks whether they understood the principles.

4. **Produce fidelity that survives actual gameplay.**  
   Blender masters, clean topology, textured materials, baked architectural lighting, selective dynamic shadows, polished animation, spatial audio, and deliberate camera composition. Progressive loading and separate quality tiers keep the experience approachable across devices. **The browser rendering is the quality standard.**

5. **Test functionality and assess the experience separately.**  
   Automated tests will cover every mission’s success, mistakes, hints, retries, saves, reloads, and recovery. They’ll also exercise missing assets, slow connections, blocked storage, rapid input, and graphics failures.

   In Codex’s internal browser, I’ll play the complete experience through visible controls, inspect every room and mascot transition, deliberately get things wrong, and test keyboard, touch layouts, muted audio, and reduced motion. Fixed screenshots and reproducible captures will document defects and their repairs.

   The visual assessment scores character, environments, teaching, interaction, accessibility/audio, and robustness. Proposed threshold: **90/100 overall, no category below 8/10, and no release-blocking defects.**

6. **Verify distribution on here.now.**  
   Publish the production build, then repeat the release journey against the actual hosted URL in a clean session. Check assets, routing, progress, downloads, and intended community access. Keep a reproducible release archive and rollback route. Authenticated permanent hosting is supported. [here.now documentation](https://here.now/docs)

“Perfect” needs observable criteria. Internal browser testing can establish substantial confidence; real community feedback and real-phone checks add evidence that this Mac cannot supply. The plan includes a small pilot and explicitly records anything unverified.

**Before the overnight build, the remaining decisions are the visual target, production authorization, and usage headroom.** Hosting authentication is handled. The first production milestone is a genuinely finished mascot and mission, establishing the standard for the entire game.
